rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken expression for moving or facing northward.

example.english: We’re walking north; the beach is that way.
example.traditional: 我哋向北行，嗰邊先係海邊。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 hoeng3 bak1 haang4 go2 bin1 sin1 hai6 hoi2 bin1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the compass direction north.

example.jyutping: zi2 naam4 zam1 zi2 zyu6 bak1

rows.note: Use this for north understood as a broad northern region or direction rather than an exact bearing.

example.english: Winters in the north are usually colder.
example.jyutping: bak1 fong1 ge3 dung1 tin1 tung1 soeng4 dung3 di1

rows.note: Use this when north means the northern part of a larger territory, such as the north of a country.

example.english: Winters in the north of Canada are very long.
example.traditional: 加拿大北部嘅冬天好長。
example.jyutping: gaa1 naa4 daai6 bak1 bou6 ge3 dung1 tin1 hou2 coeng4

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a northern location or movement toward the north, especially in compact modifiers and compounds.

example.english: Walk north from here and you'll get there.
example.jyutping: jau4 ni1 dou6 hoeng3 bak1 haang4 zau6 dou3 laa3

rows.note: Use this for the northern region or for something characterized as northern rather than for movement in a northward direction.

example.english: Winter in the north is usually colder.
example.jyutping: bak1 fong1 dung1 tin1 tung1 soeng4 dung3 di1

rows.jyutping: bak1 min6 ceoi1 lai4 ge3 N
rows.note: Use this adjectival relative-clause construction when a wind is specifically coming from the north, rather than the noun 北風.

example.english: The wind coming from the north is really cold.
example.jyutping: bak1 min6 ceoi1 lai4 ge3 fung1 hou2 dung3
